findings.text: The first lines tell a newcomer what Athena is in plain words. This works well. The rest of the page is about a different project, though, so these two sentences are all the reader learns about Athena itself.
findings.source: Athena is an open-source system, written in Rust, that turns a short request into a change to a code repository. It shows how it read the request, has one AI model do the work and a different one check it, and records what each step cost.

findings.text: This is Athena's home URL, but the title and almost every section are about firstmate. A newcomer may think they landed on the wrong site, or that Athena only writes documentation.
The page says why the study exists. It does not say why a newcomer should care about Athena, or how this study relates to Athena's main job of changing a repository from a request.
findings.source: Athena made this study of firstmate to show that it can read an unfamiliar project and explain it with every statement traced to a claim, and every claim to lines in the project's own files.

findings.text: The only clear call to action comes at the very end, after the transition cards and the glossary. The header has no link to Athena's repository, so a newcomer who stops early has nowhere to go.
findings.source: Next steps: "Learn about Athena, and how to install and try it: https://github.com/doodla/athena"

findings.text: The identifier `firstmate-work-handling` appears with no explanation. A newcomer cannot tell whether it is a file, a command, or a name.
findings.source: This page is that study of firstmate, from firstmate-work-handling.

findings.text: Some words are used but never defined: 'home', 'first mate' (as a role), 'green'/'red', and 'heartbeat'. The glossary does not cover them, so the 'Start here' section is hard to follow.
findings.source: Start here: "A secondmate is a persistent home, not a backlog item." / c37: "which stays with the main first mate"

findings.text: The glossary is long and in no clear order. Firstmate terms are mixed with terms about the page itself, so a newcomer has to scan the whole list to find a word.
'Reopened' is tagged as a terminal success. Yet the page also says the item stays open, waiting for the captain's answer. A newcomer may find that confusing.
Some source links are listed twice, and two claims are out of order. These are small, but they weaken trust in a page whose main point is careful citation.
findings.source: Claims and sources: claim-c2 lists "docs/configuration.md:357-357" twice; c14 lists "bin/fm-teardown.sh:22-23" twice; c42 lists "docs/agent-control.md:131-131" twice; c34 appears before c33

findings.text: The page is open about what it could not check, which is a strength. But terms like 'pinned tree', 'edge' and 'model-limit' are internal language a newcomer will not know.
findings.source: Limits of this study: "f1 could-not-run This study read the pinned tree only... no failure or retry edge was observed"
